account:
It is day 1, early morning, and I am at the town hall office awaiting the secretary and my appointment book. Today's remembered schedule is office at eight, a routine mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen. I still need to read the appointment book this morning; the secretary held it yesterday, and the office chest contained only her two accounts records when I checked today.

The unusual matter is yesterday's bakery chatter. The neighbour personally heard Freight offer wheat collection and bread delivery. Other talk expanded this into supposed bridge or port changes and decorations or a celebration, but the neighbour witnessed none of that, and the baker reportedly knew of no celebration. Townsfolk 02 was mentioned as a source without firsthand details. I have no evidence that these rumours describe actual plans. Freight's offer appears to concern grain and bread transport, but I do not know its wider purpose.

The builder approached this morning looking for repair work. There is no confirmed damage or approved job known to me, and I told him that inspections, repairs, and spending require prior agreement. Yesterday's treasury count was 128 emeralds, with income and expenses unverified; no money was removed. The secretary recorded that and my no-spending decision. She said she would ask the miller to prepare grain stocks and delivery records for today's routine inspection. I have not yet confirmed that this request reached the miller. No new correspondence or meeting requests had reached her as of yesterday afternoon.
